pladdrr Architecture Reference

Source: vignettes/agents/architecture.Rmd
architecture.Rmd

Version: 5.2.0 | Maintained by: coding agents and maintainers Purpose: Operational knowledge — build system, threading, dispatch patterns, stale-binary trap, compilation flags.

Dispatch Patterns

pladdrr uses three object dispatch patterns (documented v4.9.18). Each exists for a specific reason.

1. Shared Dispatch Table (Sound, Formant, Pitch, etc. — 36/39 types)

All 36 wrappers use a shared .{type}_methods environment + $.Type S3 dispatch. PraatInterpreter is the only R6Class.

.pitch_methods <- new.env(hash = TRUE, parent = emptyenv())
.pitch_methods$get_mean <- function(.self, ...) .self$.cpp$get_mean(...)
lockEnvironment(.pitch_methods, bindings = TRUE)

Pitch <- function(.xptr = NULL) {
  pitch_mod <- get_module("pitch_module")
  # The module constructor is where the pointer is reinterpreted as a Pitch; it
  # runs a Thing_isa class check, and with_pladdrr_errors() classes its refusal.
  cpp_obj <- with_pladdrr_errors(pitch_mod$RPitch$new(.xptr))
  structure(list(.xptr = .xptr, .cpp = cpp_obj), class = c("Pitch", "PraatObject"))
}

`$.Pitch` <- function(x, name) {
  val <- .subset2(x, name)       # Fast path: .xptr, .cpp
  if (!is.null(val)) return(val)
  method <- .pitch_methods[[name]]
  if (is.null(method)) return(NULL)
  function(...) method(x, ...)    # Bind self, return closure
}

Characteristics: - .self$.xptr + .self$.cpp (both present, .xptr is the external pointer to C++ Praat object) - One implementation per instance method (5.2.x): an instance getter/mutator lives in exactly one place, the Rcpp module class (src/modules/*_module.cpp), and the R method calls it as .self$.cpp$method(...). The v4.9.18 “wrapper dispatch” (.Call on .xptr for Sound/Formant/Spectrum/Spectrogram/Table queries) was reversed: it had left a second, drifting copy of each getter as an Rcpp::export in src/*_wrappers.cpp, so a fix to one copy silently did nothing. Module methods carry the guards the exports had (Praat MelderError → R error via praat_try_return, non-finite time → NA, range checks, 0 meaning whole range). - Rcpp::export is for things with no module twin: factories and converters (Sound → Pitch, …), batch/threaded routines (batch_queries.cpp), and a few shape-specific helpers (e.g. .table_to_matrix, .powercepstrogram_*). Do not add an export with the same name as a module method of the same class. Known remaining twins that are intentionally different: TextGrid get_all_points (export → data.table, module → list), Pitch/Intensity get_values_at_times (batch export vs module NA semantics). - All wrappers inherit dispatch from this pattern via $.PraatObject.

List of types using this pattern: AmplitudeTier, Cepstrum, Cochleagram, ComplexSpectrogram, Discriminant, DurationTier, Excitation, Formant, FormantGrid, FormantModeler, FormantPath, FormantTier, Harmonicity, Intensity, IntensityTier, KlattGrid, LFCC, LPC, LongSound, Ltas, MFCC, Manipulation, PraatMatrix, PCA, Pitch, PitchModule, PitchTier, PointProcess, Polygon, PowerCepstrum, Sound, Spectrogram, Spectrum, SpectrumTier, Table, TextGrid, VocalTract. (BarkSpectrogram, MelSpectrogram and DTW have no .{type}_methods table or $.Type method in NAMESPACE.)

2. Pure XPtr (PowerCepstrogram)

No .cpp object is stored — only .self$.xptr. All methods are R wrapper functions that call C++ directly via .Call(). (PowerCepstrum is not in this group: it keeps a module object like the shared-table types.) The constructor still builds an RPowerCepstrogram module object once and discards it, purely to run the class check described under “The .xptr door” below.

Why: More performant than module dispatch for these types. The shared dispatch table pattern would add unnecessary indirection for objects that only need pointer access.

3. Triple-Class + Pointer Compat (Electroglottogram)

Triple class c("Electroglottogram", "Sound", "PraatObject") + .pointer compat alias. Inherits Sound’s methods via class hierarchy.

Why: Electroglottogram is a Sound subclass in Praat’s type system. The triple class allows it to inherit Sound’s methods while maintaining its own identity.

Special Cases

  • PraatMatrix: the Praat Matrix wrapper is exported as PraatMatrix() with class c("PraatMatrix", "PraatObject"); the old name Matrix collided with the CRAN ‘Matrix’ package (duplicate function name in pkgcheck, S3 as.matrix.Matrix overwrite in R CMD check) and was removed without an alias. pladdrr registers no S3 method on a class named like another package’s class. See agent-guide.Rmd “PraatMatrix and the ‘Matrix’ package”.
  • AmplitudeTier: .pointer compat alias in $ dispatch (used by factory functions)
  • PitchTier, FormantTier, LongSound, VocalTier: static $.{type}_constructor for class methods
  • FormantPath, KlattGrid, ComplexSpectrogram: no .xptr — only .cpp stored
  • PraatInterpreter (R6): requires persistent mutable state for script execution

Threading Model

MelderThread (Praat’s Internal Pool)

Praat’s MelderThread_PARALLELIZE macro (defined in melder/MelderThread.h) is the canonical threading mechanism for all Praat vendored code. It: - Spawns threads once per parallel region - Respects pladdrr_threads() cap via MelderThread_getMaximumNumberOfConcurrentThreads() - Uses MelderThread_FOR(ielement) / MelderThread_ENDFOR blocks for per-element work - Propagates errors via _errorFlag_ atomic

IMPORTANT: MelderThread worker threads CANNOT call R API functions (Rcpp::Environment, getOption, etc.). These are not thread-safe and cause segfaults. SIMD bridge functions called from MelderThread workers must avoid R API calls.

Macro syntax — get this wrong and the file will not compile. PARALLELIZE opens its own scope and ENDFOR closes it; FOR opens the loop brace itself. Do not wrap the block in extra braces (that broke the v4.9.18 build):

MelderThread_PARALLELIZE (numberOfElements, threshold)   // no brace here
    autoVEC scratch = raw_VEC (n);                       // per-thread locals
MelderThread_FOR (ielement) {
    ...body...
} MelderThread_ENDFOR                                    // closing brace first

Thread count is platform-dependent. MelderThread_computeNumberOfThreads in src/melderthread_impl.cpp mirrors upstream’s divisors — floor(n/min) on macOS, floor(n/2/min) on Windows, round(n/1.5/min) elsewhere. Because pladdrr cannot define Praat’s macintosh macro globally (it pulls in Objective-C headers), the switch is on __APPLE__ / _WIN32 / else. Before v4.9.19 the macOS branch was hardcoded, oversubscribing Windows ~2x and Linux ~1.5x.

Partitioning is static and equal-sized. On asymmetric hardware (Apple Silicon P+E cores) that can leave the performance cores waiting on an efficiency-core straggler. Measured on an M1 Pro (8P+2E) with v4.9.19 this no longer costs anything — 10 threads is the fastest point and CPU time is flat above 8 — but the risk is latent if you change chunk sizes or thresholds.

pladdrr-added parallel regions (not upstream; Praat-tree ones logged in praat-modifications.Rmd): Sound_resample sinc branch (fon/Sound.cpp, threshold 2000 samples, per channel, 2026-10) and PowerCepstrogram_smooth_fast (batch_queries.cpp). Only add one where each element writes a disjoint output slot and reads shared input only — that keeps results bit-identical at any thread count.

How many threads “automatic” means (5.1.0). MelderThread_getNumberOfProcessors() (src/melderthread_impl.cpp) is the CPU affinity mask intersected with the cgroup CPU quota on Linux, hardware_concurrency() on macOS and Windows (job objects and macOS limits are not read), computed once per process. When _R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_ is set to anything but false — R CMD check --as-cran does — the automatic count is capped at 2, because CRAN’s timing check notes any example whose CPU time exceeds 2.5x its elapsed time. pladdrr_threads(n), n > 0, beats both. Because the count is read once, a test that depends on it needs a child process (tests/testthat/test-check-core-limit.R). The R-level default worker count (.default_n_cores()) follows the same CPU number, keeping one CPU spare only when there are more than two.

How much work a thread must get (5.1.0). The minimum frames per thread at the cepstrogram and Burg-formant sites are pladdrr constants in src/pladdrr_thread_thresholds.h (250 and 40). The earlier values (40 and 3) were below the cost of starting a thread. Remember that the divisor in MelderThread_computeNumberOfThreads differs per platform, so a threshold that keeps a short clip serial on Linux may still give it two threads on macOS.

Custom parallel_for_range (REMOVED v4.9.18)

The former custom thread pool in batch_queries.cpp (parallel_for_range template) has been replaced with MelderThread_PARALLELIZE. This eliminates: - Redundant thread creation/destruction per call - Competition between two independent thread pools - Failure to respect pladdrr_threads() cap

The .xptr door and input limits (5.1.0)

.xptr is a checked door. Every wrapper constructor that accepts .xptr ends up in an Rcpp module constructor (src/modules/*_module.cpp) that reinterprets the external pointer as its C++ struct. Each of those constructors calls require_praat_class() (src/praat_xptr_utils.h: Praat’s Thing_isa subclass test, so a Sound pointer is still accepted where Praat’s Matrix is expected, e.g. by PraatMatrix(.xptr = )), and the R side wraps the construction in with_pladdrr_errors() so the refusal arrives as a classed pladdrr_input_error (“Not a Sound (found TextGrid)”). Without the check the first field read is out of bounds and the R session dies uncatchably. A new wrapper type needs both halves; tests/testthat/test-xptr-all-constructors.R lists the types.

Sizes that become allocations are bounded. src/pladdrr_limits.h caps a Cochleagram at 2^29 cells and an Excitation at 10 000 bands; the guards sit in the vendored Sound_to_Cochleagram.cpp / Spectrum_to_Excitation.cpp (all three call doors reach them; logged in praat-modifications.Rmd). R-level factories (sound_create_tone() and siblings, PraatMatrix(), the cochleagram methods) check positive, finite and at most 2^29 cells with .check_positive_finite() / .check_cell_count() in R/validators.R. The reason is platform behaviour: asking for a 2.5 TB tensor makes Linux’s allocator fail with a Praat error, but macOS commits the pages and the kernel kills the R process (exit 137), which no tryCatch() can see.

Vendored Melder_assert is compiled out. R adds -DNDEBUG, so Praat’s ~1900 asserts, including every part()/row() bounds check, are dead code in an installed build. A missing guard therefore means silent memory corruption, not an error: validate at the pladdrr boundary. -UNDEBUG was considered and rejected (a non-NDEBUG build is 2.1-7x slower package-wide).

Test Gates

  • tests/testthat/test-fidelity-fingerprint.R runs tests/testthat/fingerprint/golden.R (81 numbers from one synthetic signal) against expected.tsv; it refuses any ERR/NA/non-finite row. Re-record only after an intended numeric change, and explain every moved key in NEWS.md.
  • tests/testthat/test-praat-faithfulness.R compares the routines in the registry with the Praat application (PLADDRR_PRAAT_EXEC, default /Applications/Praat.app/...) and, with PLADDRR_FAITHFULNESS_OUTDIR set, regenerates faithfulness-report.Rmd. Name the Praat version with any reference number: the CPPS pipeline differs between 6.4.27 and 6.4.47 by about 0.13 dB.
  • Some tests are platform-specific by nature (affinity and /proc checks are Linux-only; thread-count expectations differ per platform). A skip is not a pass: say which tests did not run.

Build System

Compilation Flags 

-O2 (CRAN floor) — default, full speed
-O3 -march=native (embedder option) — byte-identical objects, no measurable gain (see v4.9.22 in agent-guide.Rmd)
#pragma STDC FP_CONTRACT OFF in melder.h — required for bit-exactness (replaced -ffp-contract=off, 2026-08)
-DHAVE_XSIMD — unconditional; RcppXsimd is a LinkingTo dependency

-O3 -march=native does not speed this package up. A 3–7x gap was measured pre-2026-08-05, but it was the -UNDEBUG -O0 debug-build penalty from devtools::load_all()/pkgbuild::compile_dll() (see “Stale-Binary Trap” below), not the optimisation level. On a clean build, -O2 and -O3 -march=native produce byte-identical objects for the hot translation unit and are indistinguishable in wall time. Confirmed again 2026-08-06 via a clean-tarball R CMD check --as-cran with only local toolchain path-fixes (no -O3/-march=native): 0 install/check errors. Do not recommend custom flags to embedders; CRAN’s stock -O2 is full speed.

configure no longer computes a @XSIMD_FLAG@ substitution: Makevars.in set -DHAVE_XSIMD unconditionally anyway, so the detection was dead code that would have produced a confusing missing-header failure rather than a clear message. It now checks for RcppXsimd and exits with one clear error if absent.

The FLAC_SRC / MP3_SRC variables were removed in v4.9.19: they named a praat/ prefix deleted in the v4.9.5 slimming and were never referenced by SOURCES. MP3 is not decoded natively (mp3_stubs.cpp; Sound() falls back to the suggested av package). FLAC was re-vendored from Praat (libFLAC, BSD-3-Clause) and is compiled via FLAC_C_SRC in the Makevars files.

SIMD Configuration

SIMD_SRC compiles 10 *_simd*.cpp kernels/bridges plus simd_utils/simd_info (-DHAVE_XSIMD, unconditional in PKG_CPPFLAGS — RcppXsimd is a LinkingTo dependency, so the build cannot run without it). Six files with no externally referenced symbols were deleted in v4.9.19 (num_distance, num_filtering, num_matrix, pitch_processing, sound_convolution, sound_statistics — 1,174 lines). The 2026-10 audit deleted 8 more (pitch, pitch filter, autocorrelation, window functions, FormantPath, SlopeSelector, cochleagram, excitation): dead, default-off, or not bit-exact; the FormantPath kernel was a real path_finder() bug. pladdrr_simd(FALSE) gates only sound_mix/scale_peak; other SIMD paths ignore it.

Instruction set is chosen at compile time, and there is no runtime dispatch. This is the most commonly misunderstood part of the build:

Target What a stock CRAN build reaches Doubles/vector
arm64 NEON 2
x86_64 SSE2 only 2
x86_64 + -march=native in ~/.R/Makevars AVX2 / AVX-512 4 / 8

CRAN forbids -march=, and the tree contains no __attribute__((target(...))) or xsimd::dispatch. AVX2 and AVX-512 code paths are never executed by a CRAN-installed binary, whatever the CPU supports.

Measured benefit (M1 Pro, 1 s signal, single-threaded). Toggling pladdrr_simd() moves whole-routine wall time by -1% to +6%: pitch 0.99x, formant 0.98x, intensity 1.06x, spectrogram 1.03x, mfcc 1.00x, CPPS 1.00x. End-to-end analysis time is dominated by work SIMD does not touch — for CPPS, ~94% is the branchy per-frame robust trend fit. Where SIMD does pay is the batch-statistics bridges on long plain vectors (v4.9.19, after removing their input copies): mean 4.1x, sd 2.8x, range 15.4x, quantile 1.8x vs base R on 1e6 doubles.

src/simd_bridge.h is dead code — included by no translation unit. The real bridges are hand-written in src/*_simd_bridge.cpp. Edits to that header have no effect; a v4.9.18 zero-copy fix landed there and did nothing. Bridges pass R’s storage straight through as values.begin() - 1 (the same ptr - 1 idiom as Praat’s asArgumentToFunctionThatExpectsOneBasedArray()); every kernel takes const double* and none writes through it.

Static Initialisation (load-time memory)

Praat globals are linked into pladdrr.so. A big global with a non-constexpr constructor is initialised at dyn.load, dirtying every page. theForegroundPraatObjects (42 MB) did this until 2026-10 (+48 MB RSS per R process/PSOCK worker → now +7 MB). Constant-init needs both constexpr _autostring() (melder/melder_string32.h) and value-init structPraatObjects theForegroundPraatObjects {}; (sys/praat.cpp). Check with RSS before/after dyn.load when touching structPraatObjects or _autostring.

Stale-Binary Trap

tools/check_callentries.sh is wired into configure to self-heal the static→extern patch on RcppExports.cpp. Rcpp::compileAttributes() generates static by default, but src/module_init.cpp declares extern const R_CallMethodDef CallEntries[] to build a combined registration table. The patch converts static to extern in RcppExports.cpp.

Do NOT remove this patch. The combined registration table in module_init.cpp merges CallEntries + ModuleEntries into one R_registerRoutines call. R_registerRoutines REPLACES previous registrations, so both must be in a single call.

Manuscript alignment (paper/paper.md)

The JOSS manuscript carries figures that drift. Last reconciled 2026-11-11 against version 5.1.1: the manuscript now carries the package-side figures below, except the concordance statistic, which this repository cannot recompute. Re-check before each submission.

Manuscript says Package says Source of truth
38 Praat modules 39 (DESCRIPTION Description; 39 files in src/modules/) ls src/modules/*.cpp \| wc -l
“version 5.0.5” (twice) 5.1.1 DESCRIPTION
1401 tests 1587 test_that() blocks (2026-11-25) count lines matching ^\s*test_that\( in tests/testthat/*.R (the manuscript’s counting unit is not stated; use one unit)
82% coverage 93.8% (pkgcheck’s covr run, macOS aarch64, 2026-11-12; pkgcheck.log is from 5.0.5 and stale) rerun covr (see the covr FLIBS note in project memory)
CCC 0.9959 and 1.00 faithfulness-report.Rmd is the live registry: routine count, pass status and tolerances per row regenerate with the registry runner

Statements in the manuscript that hold and that these documents depend on: wrapper objects are plain lists with an external pointer and a shared per-class method environment; the interpreter is the only R6 class; SIMD and threading are gated on output identical to the scalar reference; parity with Praat outranks speed.
